note: Attacker-controlled bytes are written to a temporary file that is then opened by gf_isom_open_file, making the input the root of the parse tree.
The crafted MP4 file is parsed; the audio sample entry box (mp4a/enCa) is read via audio_sample_entry_box_read.
The base audio sample entry fields are parsed; the box size is stored in s->size and used later to scan for an embedded ESDS box.
The attacker-controlled box size is captured; this size bounds the subsequent raw-data scan for the ESDS fourcc.
Child boxes are parsed and added to ptr->child_boxes; a nested box (e.g. sinf) may also hold a reference to the same ESDS box in its own child_boxes list.
If child parsing succeeds, the function returns normally; otherwise the fallback raw-data scan below is executed.
A buffer of attacker-controlled size is allocated to hold the raw box payload for the ESDS scan.
The raw payload is scanned for the ESDS fourcc; when found, the embedded ESDS box is parsed.

The existing esd box is removed from ptr->child_boxes and freed via gf_isom_box_del; however, if the same esd pointer is also referenced in a nested child box's child_boxes list, that reference becomes dangling.
The esd box is removed from the top-level child list and its memory is freed, leaving stale pointers in any nested child_boxes lists that also reference it.
The top-level esd field is nulled, but the dangling reference inside the nested box's child_boxes list is not cleared.
A new ESDS box is parsed and assigned to ptr->esd; the old freed box remains referenced by the nested child box.
The newly parsed esd box is added to the top-level child_boxes list; the nested box still holds the freed pointer.

When the audio sample entry box is later destroyed, its nested child box is freed; that nested box's child_boxes list still contains the freed esd pointer, so gf_isom_box_del dereferences freed memory, causing the heap-use-after-free READ 8.
